text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry –  2  To ask the Minister for Education (Schools) what is being done to help deepen students' understanding of ASEAN in our mainstream schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In General Paper, students also engage in discussions about regional issues, including perspectives of ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: When investigating issues related to ASEAN and its member countries, teachers take into consideration age appropriateness, learning load and learning goals for each level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: They use authentic case studies and multiple perspectives to enable students to have a deeper understanding of these issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Schools also enhance students' appreciation of ASEAN through meaningful occasions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Students interact with their counterparts from the different member countries when they undertake overseas learning journeys in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Schools also organise ASEAN-themed forums to engage students to discuss pertinent regional and international issues.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is the Ministry now happy with the current level of awareness that our students have of ASEAN?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What is the yardstick and what does the Ministry do in terms of measurements?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Does the Ministry do surveys to see what is the current level of students' awareness?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The question is whether these are effective and what more can be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the different levels, we introduce the different sets of knowledge and discussions that we want our kids to have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the curriculum development level, we have measurements to look at how our students have grasped what they have learnt.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, as the Member can see, things are ever-changing, especially for this year, as we have assumed the Chairmanship of ASEAN.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to take this opportunity to engage our students, see how they can discuss in class and work with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to see how they can get involved in the process.
